readme.html:
Agent Skills for use with Obsidian.

These skills follow the Agent Skills specification so they can be used by any skills-compatible agent, including Claude Code, Codex, and Open Code.

Installation

Claude Code marketplace

From terminal:

claude plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
claude plugin install obsidian@obsidian-skills

From within a Claude Code session:

/plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
/plugin install obsidian@obsidian-skills

To get new skills later, run claude plugin update obsidian@obsidian-skills.

Codex marketplace

codex plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills

Then install Obsidian from the plugin directory in Codex or the ChatGPT desktop app.

Cursor

Install Obsidian from the Cursor Marketplace.

npx skills

npx skills add https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills

To use ssh instead, if you have a GitHub SSH key set up:

npx skills add git@github.com:obsidianmd/obsidian-skills.git

Manually

Claude Code

Copy the plugins/obsidian/skills/ directory to .claude/skills/ in the root of your Obsidian vault (or whichever folder you're using with Claude Code). See more in the official Claude Skills documentation.

Codex

Copy the plugins/obsidian/skills/ directory into your Codex skills path (typically ~/.agents/skills). See the Agent Skills specification for the standard skill format.

OpenCode

Clone the entire repo into the OpenCode skills directory (~/.opencode/skills/):

git clone https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills.git ~/.opencode/skills/obsidian-skills

Do not copy only the inner skills/ folder — clone the full repo so the directory structure is ~/.opencode/skills/obsidian-skills/plugins/obsidian/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md.

OpenCode auto-discovers all SKILL.md files under ~/.opencode/skills/. No changes to opencode.json or any config file are needed. Skills become available after restarting OpenCode.

Release maintenance

Update the plugin version in every manifest with:

./scripts/bump.sh patch

The script also accepts major, minor, or an explicit version like 1.1.0.

Skills

Skill Description
obsidian-markdown Create and edit Obsidian Flavored Markdown (.md) with wikilinks, embeds, callouts, properties, and other Obsidian-specific syntax
obsidian-bases Create and edit Obsidian Bases (.base) with views, filters, formulas, and summaries
json-canvas Create and edit JSON Canvas files (.canvas) with nodes, edges, groups, and connections
obsidian-cli Interact with Obsidian vaults via the Obsidian CLI including plugin and theme development
obsidian-headless Sync and publish vaults from the command line with Obsidian Headless, without the desktop app
defuddle Extract clean markdown from web pages using Defuddle, removing clutter to save tokens
knap Render Markdown templates from JSON or CSV data using Knap, including batch file generation

skills.name: defuddle
skills.description: Extract clean Markdown from HTML pages with Defuddle CLI.

skills.name: json-canvas
skills.description: Create and edit JSON Canvas files (.canvas) with nodes, edges, groups, and connections. Use when working with .canvas files, creating visual canvases, mind maps, flowcharts, or when the user mentions Canvas files in Obsidian.

skills.name: knap
skills.description: Render Markdown from templates and structured data using Knap CLI. Use when the user asks to apply a Knap template, turn JSON or CSV data into notes, batch-generate Markdown files, or format Defuddle output into a note.

skills.name: obsidian-bases
skills.description: Create and edit Obsidian Bases (.base files) with views, filters, formulas, and summaries. Use when working with .base files, creating database-like views of notes, or when the user mentions Bases, table views, card views, kanban boards, filters, or formulas in Obsidian.

skills.name: obsidian-cli
skills.description: Interact with Obsidian vaults using the Obsidian CLI to read, create, search, and manage notes, tasks, properties, and more. Also supports plugin and theme development with commands to reload plugins, run JavaScript, capture errors, take screenshots, and inspect the DOM. Use when the user asks to in

skills.name: obsidian-headless
skills.description: Sync and publish Obsidian vaults from the command line with Obsidian Headless (`ob`), without the desktop app. Use when the user wants to set up or run Obsidian Sync or Obsidian Publish on a server, in CI, or from a terminal, or change a vault's Sync or Publish settings.

skills.name: obsidian-markdown
skills.description: Create and edit Obsidian Flavored Markdown with wikilinks, embeds, callouts, properties, and other Obsidian-specific syntax. Use when working with .md files in Obsidian, or when the user mentions wikilinks, callouts, frontmatter, tags, embeds, or Obsidian notes.
